turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Well, thanks for seeing me. Um, what brings me in... I guess it's just that I can't seem to keep my mind on a task long enough to actually finish it anymore. Even when it's really important. Like, I'm a computer support specialist, right? And I'll be trying to trace a client's network problem, which usually isn't that hard if you just follow the steps, but ten minutes into it, I'll realize I've just stared at the same log entries three times over. I won't even know what they say. It's like my brain just... goes somewhere else. Which reminds me, the other day I was looking at this one log file and I noticed the timestamp was off by exactly three hours and twelve minutes. It made me think about this trip I took to Iceland a few years ago. Have you ever been? The time difference really messes with you, but the hot springs are amazing. We rented this little car and drove the Ring Road, and... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the network logs. Yeah, I just can't focus on them anymore. It's really becoming a problem at work.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly states they cannot keep their mind on a task long enough to finish it, such as staring at the same log entries without comprehending them.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates being easily distracted by unrelated thoughts, going off on a tangent about a trip to Iceland after seeing a timestamp, and losing their train of thought.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized or high and needed much less sleep than usual?
turns.patient_response:
Energized? No, not really. I mean, I don't get high or anything, and I definitely need my sleep. Actually, speaking of sleep, I just bought one of those new cooling memory foam mattresses last month. The reviews online were incredible, but getting it delivered was an absolute nightmare. The delivery guys couldn't get the box up my stairs because my house was built in the twenties and it has this really sharp turn right at the landing. It's a beautiful old house, lots of original woodwork, but it is just terrible for moving modern furniture. 

I actually had to take the whole banister off just to get the mattress box up there. Have you ever tried to remove screws that have been painted over for a hundred years? It's impossible. I had to drive down to the hardware store, the local one over on 4th street, and buy a special extractor bit. The guy working there was telling me about his own home renovations, and he used this specific type of wood stain that... wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling energized and not sleeping. Yeah, no, I don't think I've ever had a period like that. I usually just try to get my regular eight hours.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets distracted by a chain of unrelated thoughts about a mattress and home repairs, temporarily losing track of the doctor's question.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient talks excessively, going on a long, detailed tangent about a mattress delivery and hardware store before answering the question.
symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient explicitly denies ever feeling 'high' or having periods of elevated mood.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient explicitly denies having periods where they felt unusually 'energized'.
symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient explicitly denies needing less sleep, stating they definitely need their sleep and try to get their regular eight hours.

turns.doctor_question: Did these focus problems begin when you were a child?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, actually, they did. My mom still brings it up, usually at Thanksgiving when everyone's around. She jokes that my grade school report cards always said the exact same thing—that I was a bright kid but I could never just stay in my seat. I was always blurting out answers before the teacher even finished the question, and I'd lose my homework all the time, even when I actually did it. 

Which is so frustrating, right? Doing the work and then not getting credit for it. It reminds me of this time in college, I wrote this massive paper on the history of early computing—like, ENIAC and punch cards and all that. Did you know the first programmers were actually women? They called them "computers" back then. It's fascinating stuff. Anyway, I spent weeks on this paper, printed it out at the library because my printer was out of ink—it was one of those old dot-matrix ones where you had to tear the perforated edges off the paper. I loved the sound those things made. But yeah, I printed it, put it in my bag, and somehow between the library and the lecture hall, it just... vanished. I had to beg the professor for an extension. He was this older guy, always wore these tweed jackets with the elbow patches. I wonder if professors still wear those? I haven't been on a campus in years... wait, what was I saying? 

Oh, right, being a kid. Yeah, the focus stuff and losing things, that's been happening pretty much my whole life.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient confirms that 'focus stuff' (focus problems) has been happening their whole life.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient explicitly mentions losing their homework all the time in grade school and losing a major paper in college.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility during the response by going on a long tangent about unrelated thoughts and losing their train of thought.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient recalls that their grade school report cards noted they could never stay in their seat.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient states they were always blurting out answers before the teacher finished the question.
